items.title: Jurassic Park's T. rex had a real problem
source_notes: Amblin official film page: https://amblin.com/movie/jurassic-park/ — confirms the production combined CGI dinosaurs with full-scale animatronics.

ABC News retrospective: https://abcnews.com/Entertainment/jurassic-park-turns-25-scenes-moments-iconic-summer/story?id=55332468 — reports the rain caused problems for the T. rex animatronic and crew dried it between takes.

scenes.text: Jurassic Park's terrifying T. rex had a surprisingly real problem.
The 1993 film mixed computer-generated dinosaurs with a huge physical animatronic built by Stan Winston's effects team.
During the famous rainstorm scene, water soaked into the dinosaur's skin and caused problems for the mechanism.
The crew had to dry the T. rex between takes. Sometimes, practical movie magic needs a towel.

items.title: Jurassic Park barely shows its dinosaurs
source_notes: ABC News, cast and crew retrospective: https://abcnews.com/Entertainment/jurassic-park-turns-25-scenes-moments-iconic-summer/story?id=55332468 — reports crew members estimated about 15 minutes of dinosaur footage in the 2-hour-7-minute film.

scenes.text: Here's a Jurassic Park trick you might never have noticed.
The 1993 movie runs for about two hours and seven minutes.
But cast and crew members told ABC News the dinosaurs appear for only about fifteen minutes in total.
That scarcity makes every dinosaur reveal feel like an event. Sometimes, showing less makes a monster feel bigger.

items.title: Jurassic Park's T. rex was too big for the building
source_notes: ABC News, cast and crew retrospective: https://abcnews.com/Entertainment/jurassic-park-turns-25-scenes-moments-iconic-summer/story?id=55332468 — reports the team modified the workshop building to accommodate the huge T. rex animatronic; crew member estimates its final dimensions.

scenes.text: Jurassic Park's T. rex caused a real construction problem.
Stan Winston's effects team was building a giant physical dinosaur for the 1993 film.
According to crew members interviewed by ABC News, the team had to modify the building—raising the roof and enlarging a door—to move the enormous creation.
The behind-the-scenes challenge was almost as huge as the dinosaur itself.

items.title: A real hurricane interrupted Jurassic Park
source_notes: ABC News, cast and crew retrospective: https://abcnews.com/Entertainment/jurassic-park-turns-25-scenes-moments-iconic-summer/story?id=55332468 — reports Hurricane Iniki struck Kauai on September 11, 1992 while the production was filming in Hawaii.

scenes.text: Jurassic Park faced a real-life disaster during production.
The crew was filming on Hawaii's island of Kauai in 1992.
ABC News reports that Hurricane Iniki struck on September 11, forcing cast and crew members to take shelter.
The movie's fictional island was dangerous enough. The real weather brought its own drama.

items.title: The T. rex water-cup ripple had a real inspiration
source_notes: Cinemablography production-history article: https://www.cinemablography.org/blog/behind-the-scenes-jurassic-park-t-rex-entrance-scene — recounts Spielberg's idea for the vibrating water cup after seeing bass music vibrate a car's rear-view mirror; cross-check against production feature material before publishing.

scenes.text: That tiny ripple in the Jurassic Park water cup was designed to build fear.
Before the T. rex appears, the water begins to tremble with its approaching footsteps.
A production-history account says Steven Spielberg got the idea after noticing loud bass music vibrate his car's rear-view mirror.
One small ripple warns the audience about a giant threat before they even see it.
